sec: Hypertension 2023 · resistant-hypertension options and special scenarios

items.q: Three of these are listed as other options for resistant hypertension. Which one is not?
items.exp: The other options block lists beta-blockers, prazosin, clonidine and renal denervation, the last being the procedural entry among the drug choices. (Book p981)

items.q: Fill up: In coronary artery disease the page starts with ______, adds ______ for the angina patient, and offers ______ for the non-angina patient.
opts: A plus B; C; C or D
A plus C; B; C or D
A plus B; D; B only
C plus D; A; B only
items.exp: The CAD branch begins with A plus B, then splits into adding C for angina and adding C or D for non-angina patients. (Book p981)

items.q: Match each special scenario with the opening regimen printed under it — 1) Coronary artery disease 2) Chronic kidney disease with eGFR above 30 3) Chronic kidney disease with eGFR at or below 30 … A) A plus C, then add D, then spironolactone if uncontrolled B) A plus B, then C or D depending on angina C) A plus C, then chlorthalidone, then a beta-blocker if uncontrolled
items.exp: CAD opens on A plus B, while both CKD arms start with A plus C and then divide by eGFR, the lower band escalating through chlorthalidone to a beta-blocker and the higher band through a thiazide-like diuretic to spironolactone. (Book p981)

items.q: A patient with CKD stage G4 has a BP of 152/92 mmHg on telmisartan and amlodipine. Which add-on does the CKD flowchart require?
opts: A beta-blocker as the immediate next drug
items.exp: An eGFR at or below 30 takes the left CKD branch, where the add-on is chlorthalidone and a beta-blocker only follows if control is still not achieved. (Book p981)

items.q: Assess the right-hand CKD branch: I With an eGFR above 30 the add-on is D, and spironolactone follows only when control is still not achieved. II This branch mirrors the resistant-hypertension rule that a thiazide-like diuretic is reserved for preserved filtration.
items.exp: The above-30 limb runs A plus C, add D, then add spironolactone if uncontrolled, but the page never states a general rule reserving thiazides for preserved filtration, and on the previous page chlorthalidone is precisely the low-eGFR partner. (Book p981)

items.q: A 63-year-old with stable angina has repeated clinic readings of 154/94 mmHg. Which regimen and escalation does this page map out?
opts: Start A plus B, then add C for the angina
Start A plus C, then add D
Start C plus D, then add spironolactone
Start A plus C, then chlorthalidone
items.exp: Coronary artery disease is the left-hand special scenario, opening with A plus B, and because the patient has angina the next arrow is the addition of C. (Book p981)

items.q: Which statement misreads the two CKD branches on this page?
opts: Both branches begin with A plus B
The other branch escalates to D
Both branches begin with A plus C
items.exp: Every CKD patient starts on A plus C, and the split by eGFR decides whether chlorthalidone or D is the add-on, so a claim of a shared A plus B start is the false statement. (Book p981)

items.q: Which eGFR value separates the two escalation routes in the CKD scenario?
items.exp: The fork is printed as eGFR at or below 30 versus above 30 mL/min, the same boundary used for spironolactone in resistant hypertension on the previous page. (Book p981)

items.q: Fill up: In the low-eGFR CKD branch, failure of chlorthalidone leads to adding a ______, whereas in the high-eGFR branch failure of D leads to adding ______.
items.exp: The two not-controlled arrows are drawn to a beta-blocker below an eGFR of 30 and to spironolactone above it. (Book p981)

items.q: How many distinct special scenarios are laid out on this page?
opts: Two, coronary artery disease and chronic kidney disease
Three, adding heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
Four, adding aortic stenosis and diabetes
items.exp: The special scenarios heading carries exactly two trees, CAD on the left and CKD on the right. (Book p981)
